title: Bourgain notable-coordinate structure
statement: There exist positive real constants $C,D$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every real-valued function $f$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, define $k=I(f)/\varepsilon$, where $I(f)$ is the total influence. There is a choice of a set of coordinates $J(x)$ for each outcome $x$ such that, for every $x$, $|J(x)|\leq e^{Ck}$ and the number of subsets $S\subseteq J(x)$ with $|S|\leq k$ is at most $e^{Dk^2}$; moreover, the expectation of the sum of squared components $f_S(x)^2$ over all subsets $S\subseteq[n]$ not in that family is at most $2\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist real constants C and D with 0 < C and 0 < D
Product P of n finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and coordinate weights summing to one
Function f takes only the values −1 and 1
k is total influence I(f) divided by ε
replaced: There are absolute $C,D>0$ such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, putting $k=I(f)/\varepsilon$, there exist sets $J(x)\subseteq[n]$ satisfying $|J(x)|\le e^{Ck}$ and $|\{S\subseteq J(x):|S|\le k\}|\le e^{Dk^2}$ for every $x$, and $\mathbb E_P\sum_{S\notin\{T\subseteq J(x):|T|\le k\}}f_S(x)^2\le2\varepsilon$.
